journey.name: Signup — a paid-for token survives the app dying
journey.description:
The invariant that costs real money if it breaks. A signup token is single-use and never expires, and by the time Loopky holds one the user has already spent an SMS attempt (two per week) or paid sats. If the app is killed between obtaining the token and Ring redeeming it, the token must still be there on the next launch — otherwise they pay twice.
Requires the same setup as `17-signup-invite-code.xml`, and a freshly minted staging token.
This journey deliberately never completes the hand-off, so the token it uses stays unspent and can be reused for the next run — unlike journey 17, which burns one.

actions.action: From a signed-out Loopky, tap "onboarding_create_pubky", then "signup_method_invite"
Tap "signup_invite_input", type a freshly minted XXXX-XXXX-XXXX token, tap "signup_invite_submit"
When Pubky Ring opens, DO NOT authorize. Press back to return to Loopky
Verify Loopky is on the hand-off screen: "signup_title" reads "Finishing in Pubky Ring…"
Kill the app outright: adb shell am force-stop com.github.jvsena42.loopky
Relaunch: adb shell am start -n com.github.jvsena42.loopky/.MainActivity
Verify logcat shows "init: no persisted session" — signing up never completed, so there is no session

Navigate to the hand-off again (onboarding_create_pubky is the entry; the stored token is what the hand-off resumes from) and verify "signup_handoff_copy" is present — the token survived the process being killed

Tap "signup_handoff_copy" and verify the toast "Code copied — keep it somewhere safe", then paste elsewhere and confirm the value matches the token that was minted. A token the user can read cannot be lost to a bug in the app

THE WRONG-PUBKY BRANCH, if it can be provoked. When Ring's signup fails while it holds another already-signed-up pubky, Ring quietly authorizes THAT pubky instead and returns a valid session with the token unspent

Verify that in this case Loopky still shows "signup_handoff_copy" — i.e. the token was NOT cleared. Clearing on "we got a session" would throw away something the user paid for in exactly the case where they still need it. logcat shows "onApproved: signed in on a different homeserver — keeping the token"
